rationale: Unsupported format throws before the guarded path; no supplied mapper converts it to documented 422. The unhandled exception is an implementation fault under §9.3 R1.

PUT omits requestBody while binding requires Secret. The client supplies a body but does not establish omitted-body policy; no independent scenario-specific intent evidence resolves which artifact is wrong.

Nullable persist is unboxed into a primitive without validation or fallback. Null therefore reaches an internal-error path; §9.3 R1 attributes this to implementation. Persist is neither a resource key nor a mandatory persistent field.

Optional dates pass validation as null but are unconditionally parsed, producing an unhandled null failure. The URI generator already supports absent dates. §9.3 R1 attributes the crash to implementation.

The search handler returns a results/pagination wrapper. Its integration test explicitly asserts results and page links for this GET. Independent field-level evidence makes the single-mandate response annotation incorrect.

The converter rejects unknown enum values, but throwing IllegalArgumentException does not establish the HTTP result. Local tests/docs do not resolve this query-binding branch or demonstrate a contract violation; intent attribution remains unsupported.

Create-payment prose and its integration test explicitly require payment_id. The actual unwrapped Payment serializes that name; Swagger documents paymentId from a separate documentation DTO. The contract property name is wrong.

Optional.of rejects missing dates before its fallback can run in the special-product branch. Optional date filters could use the existing now fallback; this deterministic null crash is an implementation fault under §9.3 R1.

The empty-tag branch deliberately omits the documented JSON body. Its test uses ten tags, so it does not establish empty-list intent. The separate all-tags operation cannot settle this branch; neither artifact has independent decisive support.

Office formatting changes the body but leaves the configured JSON content type. Independent controllers set media type for each selected format, supporting the contract policy. Missing response-type assignment is an implementation fault.

The 204 branches handle missing versions, not descriptor-type filtering. No independent test/doc establishes their intended status. Two branches in one method do not corroborate intent; the proposition does not establish the claimed scenario equivalence.

The success body is Tan, while the documented wrapper is open and has no required properties. Tests assert only status; prose says return TAN without specifying JSON structure. Independent evidence does not establish the claimed response-shape obligation.

Refund creation tests deliberately supply refund_amount_available, including its mismatch scenario. The service consumes it as request precondition data. Independent request-field evidence contradicts the response-only annotation; the contract is overly restrictive.

The validator uses find with a dollar anchor, allowing a match before a final line feed. Independent documentation requires SHA-256 GUID hashes and a 64-character representation. This accepts a syntactically invalid key at validation.

The null guard returns 400, but the optional parameter also documents default available. No supplied test proves omission binds null or establishes null-branch intent. A guard alone cannot attribute a failure; framework default binding remains unobserved.

The contract promises a user-session office default, but requiredParam throws for absent or empty query values before retrieval. This violates the documented default under §10.7, so primary attribution is implementation.

GET /projects integration fixtures and assertions treat score as Integer, consistent with numeric scoring tests and the returned entity. Independent endpoint-linked evidence supports the implementation’s numeric model; the string contract type should change.

The endpoint passes null through the processor to getReturnUrl, which dereferences request before the StripeException catch. Authorized session creation therefore contains a deterministic implementation crash; no contract change is needed.
